title: 4GE1-style exam questions: physical fieldwork enquiry design and data collection (Paper 1, Section B)
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y11 lesson 25 (Own 4GE1-style exam questions with indicative mark points (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 25: Revision: physical fieldwork enquiry design and data collection (Paper 1, Section B). Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: Exam-style Section B questions on the portal: justify a sampling method, describe a technique, explain one risk and how it was reduced, suggest one secondary source.
questions.a: Indicative mark points in the portal key
questions.model: Teacher does the first 3-marker: 'Justify your sampling method': name it (systematic, every 50 m), how it worked, and why it suited the aim (even coverage of the river's length).

questions.q: Explain how one technique could give unreliable data and how to improve it.
questions.a: For example: float method affected by wind (1); repeat three times and use the mean (1); use a flow meter (1)

questions.q: Explain why both quantitative and qualitative data strengthen an enquiry.
questions.a: Numbers allow analysis and comparison (1); sketches and photos explain context and processes (1); together they support stronger conclusions (1)

questions.q: Calculate discharge: width 3.0 m, mean depth 0.4 m, velocity 0.4 m/s.
questions.a: Area = 3.0 x 0.4 = 1.2 m2 (1); discharge = 1.2 x 0.4 = 0.48 cumecs (1)
questions.model: Step 1: cross-sectional area = width x mean depth = 3.0 x 0.4 = 1.2 m2. Step 2: discharge = area x velocity = 1.2 x 0.4 = 0.48 m3/s (cumecs).

questions.q: Write a hypothesis for a river enquiry.
questions.a: For example: Channel width increases with distance downstream

questions.q: Name two secondary sources for a river enquiry.
questions.a: For example: Environment Agency river level data and an OS map (or geology map, rainfall data)

questions.q: Big question: what makes a fieldwork enquiry trustworthy?
questions.a: A clear hypothesis, suitable sampling, accurate and repeated measurements, safe methods and more than one data source
